messages.content: 了解しました。どのような変更をコミットしますか？まず、`git status` を実行して現在の変更状況を確認します。

thoughts.subject: Planning the Commit Process
thoughts.description: I'm starting with a plan to guide the commit process. First, I will check the repository's status to understand the changes. Then, a diff check against the HEAD commit will reveal specifics. Finally, reviewing the recent log will provide context.

thoughts.subject: Outlining Commit Execution
thoughts.description: I've refined the initial plan further. After checking the repo's status and reviewing the `git diff` output, I will examine the commit history with `git log -n 3` to mirror its style. Following this, I'll generate a tentative commit message, ensuring the user can review it before committing. I'll start by executing the status check now.

thoughts.subject: Debugging the Command
thoughts.description: I'm now working on correcting the parameter error I made when attempting to run `git status`. The `description` parameter needs to be a string, not `None`. After I've corrected it, I'll rerun the command to check the status.

thoughts.subject: Restarting Git Status
thoughts.description: I've corrected the parameter error, ensuring the `description` is a string, and am ready to re-execute `git status`. Following a successful status check, my next steps involve examining the differences with `git diff HEAD` and reviewing recent commit history. Then, I'll formulate a commit message.

thoughts.subject: Reviewing the Modifications
thoughts.description: I've just examined the output of `git status` and identified the modified files. Now, the next logical step is to inspect the specific changes within each file. I'll likely employ `git diff` on the listed files to understand what I need to commit.

thoughts.subject: Inspecting the Changes
thoughts.description: I've executed `git diff HEAD` and am now poring over the changes. I've got the output in front of me, looking at the specifics. Alongside that, I am running `git log -n 3` to gain insights into the preferred commit style. Soon, I'll draft the commit message, pending user confirmation.
